My /code-review medium on round 3 (c085892..d10eb90).

An IPv4-mapped or IPv4-compatible IPv6 literal is its IPv4 address, on
either side of the comparison: with 10.0.0.5 denied, ::ffff:10.0.0.5,
::ffff:a00:5 and ::10.0.0.5 reached it, and a mapped address in
--redisUrl did not deny the plain one. The same reading makes
::127.0.0.1 a loopback literal.

A denied socket path is compared as the connect reaches it: a relative
path from the process's directory, read once at load (workers cannot
chdir, and the namespace later answers process.cwd() with /app), with
., .. and // resolved. A symlink or hard link to the socket is not
caught until the network broker, now said in security-model.md.

The marker of net.connect's normalised arguments is taken from
net._normalizeArgs, which net.connect uses, not by standing in for
Socket.prototype.connect at load. One helper reads the marker, both to
detect the array and to copy it. The UDP handle capture accepts only an
object whose handle can open and bind.

Docs: security-model.md's Redis bullet; CHANGELOG.

Tests: test/sandbox/38 (the IPv6 forms both ways, the IPv4-compatible
loopback, the socket-path spellings).
RED: on d10eb90's lockdown, 38 gave 3 failing (::ffff:10.0.0.5,
::ffff:a00:5, ::10.0.0.5 and the plain form of a mapped configured
address not denied; ::127.0.0.1 and ::7f00:2 not denied; .., //, ./ and
a relative path not denied).
GREEN: lint clean; full npm test (test/sandbox 34, 38 included): 1267 passing, 10 pending, 0 failing.

/code-review high on #37 (seven findings, two blocking).

  whatever its code. It used to strip a module's own code to a plain
  Error (no code, origin or details), so the whole envelope reached a
  composing module only when the callee broke §5.1 with a catalogue-named
  code. composition/17 now expects the full module error for the own-code
  case in all three modes. composition/15's made-up-code case (16b80f3's
  rule: a callee's non-catalogue code was a callee crash to the
  composite's caller) now expects the callee's code, NOT_A_RUNTIME_CODE,
  on both paths; the comment at lib/service-client.js's hop boundary says
  so.
- fail()'s toJSONSafeFault is total: `throw null` and `Promise.reject()`
  used to throw inside it, so the async call was never answered (the

  realm): a thrown plain object with a code is a crash, not a typed

Review of #36 (the reviewer's /code-review high and my /code-review
medium on both rounds).

Descriptors. net.connect and net.createConnection (one function) build
Node's internal Socket, not the exported net.Socket the guard wraps, so
connect({fd}) adopted the descriptor in every mode. Without --hardened
the native open(fd) backstop still caught it; under --hardened nothing
did, so a module could take the main server's listening socket. An http
request given an fd reaches the same route through the agent. Both are
now checked at their entry (https goes through tls.connect, which reads
no fd).

Under --hardened, open(fd) on a TCP, Pipe or UDP handle a module built
from an instance's constructor was not guarded at all before this
release: the backstop's prototypes came from process.binding, which the
permission model refuses. The lockdown now takes them from instances it
builds before any module code runs, with no syscall (a Socket's connect
builds its handle before it validates an invalid port or path, and a
setter on the instance sees it; a dgram socket's handle has no socket
until bind), and destroys them. A kind it cannot take refuses the load
under enforce and is logged under audit, as the lockdown's own state,
not a violation by the module.

Each guarded entry (net.Socket, net.connect, Socket#connect,
tls.connect, server.listen, dgram bind) copies its options object once,
inherited enumerable properties included, checks the copy and passes it
on, so a getter cannot answer the check undefined and Node a number.
dgram bind and net.connect take a bare number as a port, so they check
the fd option only.

The Redis denial reads the host as Node will connect to it. An empty
host is localhost. Both sides are compared in their canonical spelling,
so 10.5 is 10.0.0.5 and fd00:0:0::5 is fd00::5. Every loopback literal
counts: all of 127/8, 0.0.0.0, ::1 and ::, in every form the resolver
accepts (127.1, 2130706433), and IPv4-mapped. So do the loopback names
(localhost, *.localhost, localhost.localdomain, ip6-localhost,
ip6-loopback), not six fixed spellings. A path counts as a pipe only
when it is truthy, as in Node.

server.listen stays strict about handles, now said in a comment.

Docs: security-model.md's adoption and Redis bullets; CHANGELOG
Security, including that the raw handle's open was reachable under
--hardened before this release, and that a module requiring _tls_wrap
or _tls_common now fails to load.

Tests: test/sandbox/36 (the capture under --permission; no descriptor
but libuv's /dev/null reserve; the enforce refusal and the audit
report), test/sandbox/37 (empty host, spellings, inherited options),
09 (the getter form; net.connect, createConnection and http.request
with an fd; open(fd) on each handle kind; one server), 34 (the loopback
literals and names), 05 (connectFd; the handle case reads only the log
since its call), 35 (the no-violation check waits for the log); the
fetch probe gives up after 5 s. A shared helper,
test/helpers/lockdown-worker.js, installs the lockdown in a worker.
RED, on f9a41e8..c085892's lockdown: 09, 34 and 36 gave 8 failing
(09: the getter form adopted the descriptor, connect({fd}) reached
Node's fd adoption, a TCP handle's open(fd) was allowed; 34: 127.0.0.2
reached Redis in both modes; 36: all three). 37 gave 3 failing before
its fix (an empty host, the spellings, inherited options). GREEN: 05,
09 and 34-37 give 154 passing, 2 pending. Full npm test: 1257 passing,
10 pending, 2 failing, all in test6, the single-thread benchmark,
which loads no lockdown. 100 of its 100000 requests hung up under load,
and test7 did not run after it. test6 and test7 re-run: 4 passing, 0
errors.

Step 1 (d2) of the logger-and-errors spec, from /code-review medium on
the previous commit.

- The foreign-code list's TLS part is an exact list, not prefixes (the
  reviewer, 2026-11-10): the prefixes missed real codes (INVALID_CA,

  plus HOSTNAME_MISMATCH (each checked present in the v24.22.2 and
  v26.13.0 binaries); test/validation/05 pins it, with a note to re-check
  it when the Node floor moves. llhttp's HPE_ prefix (a malformed HTTP
  response) joins the list.
- CountinghouseError.replyFields is the one encoder for every reply
  between threads: sendMessageToParent and the main thread's runtime-error
  replies to a composing worker used hand-built fields; worker-message's
  alias wrappers go, and validation/05 tests the shared encoder.
- A latent bug: replyFields gave errMsg undefined for a message-less or
  non-Error err, which every receiver reads as success. errMsg is now
  always a string.
- fromModule's doc comment, split by the foreign-code block, is whole
  again; the comments and the spec say countinghouse-validate will read
  the list (step 1 (e)), not that it does.

unchanged.

R2-1 part 2 (spec "The always-denied set"). Under audit and under
enforce a module can no longer read the auth configuration (the JSON
file under --authProvider file; the sqlite database with its -wal, -shm
and -journal side files), nor the identity secret under
--moduleDataPath, however it names them: directly, through a symlink in
its /tmp, through `..`, or through a hard link in a declared rw
directory, and after the file is rewritten in place. The answer is
EACCES, ahead of the ENOENT enforce gives any other outside path, and
the server records `module sandbox: <name> file denied <target>`. Off
decides nothing and is unchanged.

lib/fs-broker/denied.js (new) knows the files by real path and, once
they exist, by (dev, ino), refreshed at most once a second; a path that
does not exist yet is matched by its name in its real parent. The
broker consults it for an outside path (resolved on the host even under
audit, the one cost an outside access now pays there) and for a path
inside the namespace after checkHost has resolved the real location.

COUNTINGHOUSE_* never reaches a worker's environment even when a module
declares it: the load logs `env <NAME> denied` and the validator warns
(stage countinghouse.permissions) that the declaration has no effect.

The worker's options carry neither redisUrl nor dbUrl
(cli-options.getOptionsForWorker; the main-thread defaults for both no
longer apply in a worker), and the Redis endpoint is refused inside the
worker with EACCES from net.connect, tls.connect and a raw Socket, under
every loopback name, in audit as in enforce, through one wrap on
net.Socket.prototype.connect; the violation line reads `violation redis
<host>:<port> (blocked)`. An in-worker check until the network broker
ships. Dropping dbUrl with redisUrl is a Task 2 ruling agreed in review;
the spec is amended in this commit.

From the review of the identity service (R2-1 Task 1, previous commit):

The key never stands in for the user name. rebuild() and the file
provider's entries() fell back to the key for an entry without a
userName, so /identity-lookup ("never the key") and every record that
carries userName would have handed it out. Both fall back to null; the
route and the tool answer userName null, and the tool's outputSchema
allows it.

The id index is built before the server listens: framework.js runs the
serving half (the RouteManager listens from its constructor) only once
identity.rebuild resolves, so a user with a stable id never gets a
key-based id from an early call with sqlite or CouchDB; a provider that
cannot answer at startup refuses the start with exit 2, naming the
provider and never a key. rebuild() refuses two entries yielding one id,
naming positions.

The secret lives under the data directory, so an unusable
--moduleDataPath refuses startup too: exit 2, "--moduleDataPath <path>
cannot be created or is not writable: set it to a writable directory",
never the secret. It used to fail each module load instead (CI found
fs-broker/09 broken by the previous commit); the case is rewritten to
assert the new behaviour. Two servers started at once on an empty data
directory would each generate a secret; the upgrade guide says to start
one first.

test/auth/31: an entry with no userName resolves to null through the
route and the tool, with no key in either answer; a corrupt sqlite
database makes the start exit 2; a duplicate stable id in entries()
makes rebuild reject naming entries 1 and 2 and no key; with sqlite a
stable id resolves on the first call after the server is ready. Failed
before (the key stood in; the corrupt start reached ready; the duplicate
rebuild resolved), pass now; the full suite passes.

IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND joins lib/error-catalogue.js (kind caller, not
retryable, 500, no MCP code; the texts the error-info tables carry),
since master now reads codes from the catalogue (c605203) and
validation/04 requires every code lib/ raises to be in it.

R2-1 Task 1. Every user gets an opaque id, "u_" and 22 characters of
base64url(HMAC-SHA256(secret, source)), the same across every module on
this server. The source is the auth entry's optional stable `id` field
("id:" + field) when it has one, else the API key ("key:" + apiKey):
domain-separated, so an id equal to another user's key never yields that
user's id. With a stable id a key rotation keeps the user's id; without
one the id changes with the key.

lib/identity.js: initSync loads or creates the secret -- 32 random bytes
as 64 hex characters in <moduleDataPath>/.identity-secret (0600, written
under a temporary name and renamed, never read through a link, refused if
group- or world-readable) or COUNTINGHOUSE_IDENTITY_SECRET in the same
form; a variable in another form, or a file and a variable that differ,
refuse startup with exit 2 and never echo a value. The index
(id -> {apiKey, userName, isAdmin}) is built from provider.entries() at
startup and on every reload, and never leaves the main thread (every call
throws in a worker). lookup() is synchronous for the billing hot path;
resolve() asks the provider once more on a miss, at most every 5 s.

Providers: entries() on file, sqlite and CouchDB; the file provider checks
the id field (1-128 printable characters, unique) at startup -- two entries
sharing one exit 2, "<path>: entries 2 and 5 share id", never a key --
and on reload; sqlite adds a nullable `id` column (unique where set) on
open, and bin/countinghouse-auth-sqlite.js gets `set-id <apiKey> <id>`,
which adds the column too (the CLI opens the database itself); CouchDB reads
the id as the view's 5th value when the design document emits one (the one
init-db installs emits four, so users fall back to their key until it is
re-run; untested against a live CouchDB here).

The operator's lookup: POST /identity-lookup {id} (admin only) and the
authoring tool countinghouse_lookup_identity answer {id, userName,
isAdmin} or IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND (new, both locales), never the key.
POST /reload-auth and its tool rebuild the index after a reload.

Everything that named a tenant by its key moves to the id: the key
fingerprint in log lines is `id u_...` on a started main thread (the old
sha256 prefix before init and in workers); a repeatable job's scheduler id
is <id>:<name>, and removal still finds a scheduler stored under the old
owner prefix. Under --debug the debug key is indexed as {userName:
'debug', isAdmin: true}.

- module faults validated against the action's fault schema and delivered;

CI now tests the newest 26.x beside 24.15.0 and the newest 24.x; the
supported floor (engines, lib/node-version.js) stays 24.15. A workflow
concurrency group cancels a pull request's superseded run on a new push
(grouped by PR number) and never cancels a master run (grouped by sha).

Two Node 26 findings, fixed here:
- Node 26 adds fs.openAsBlobSync, which the worker's file patch did not
  cover: on Node 26 module code could read a host path through it under
  every --moduleSandbox mode (shown by test/fs-broker/23 before this
  change: it stat'd the host's /data/f.txt). It is brokered like
  openAsBlob (the sync read through the broker, wrapped in a Blob with its
  type) and installed only where Node has it, so Node 24 gains no method.
- Node 26's permission model adds a network permission: under --hardened
  the relaunched server could neither listen nor reach Redis (fs-broker/14's
  --hardened cases). hardened-launch now passes --allow-net where
  process.allowedNodeEnvironmentFlags has it, so the network stays
  unrestricted under --hardened, as on Node 24, until the network broker.
  Node's ExperimentalWarning for the flag is left visible.
- Node 26 adds the built-in node:ffi (native calls from JavaScript). It was
  already refused to module code (the allowlist is a literal); it is now
  classified explicitly as refused, which sandbox/05's "accounts for every
  built-in" check requires. Under --hardened, Node's permission model
  refuses ffi.dlopen too (it needs --allow-ffi, never passed; --allow-addons
  does not cover it), noted in security-model.md beside --allow-addons.

Nothing serialized an operator's load, reload, restart and unload of one
module. A second reload arriving while the first one's worker was still
coming up spawned alongside it; the lifecycle lock then terminated the
first worker, whose load answered "worker ended while loading", and the
first reload settled the module's devices to MODULE_UNLOADED, failing the
jobs waiting through the reload for good, though the second worker was
about to come up. An unload arriving in that window found no module
registered, was refused as "unknown module", and was then undone by the
reload's worker coming up.

Each operator action on a name now steps a generation, and only the
latest is in force. A reload superseded while its worker comes up ends
that worker (the lifecycle lock terminates it when the next spawn takes
its turn, or the unload does; a spawn still queued never starts), settles
nothing, and answers its caller MODULE_LOAD_SUPERSEDED, a new code. An
operator unload during a reload cancels it: with the worker already being
ended by the reload, the end becomes an unload (endingFor 'unload', the
devices MODULE_UNLOADED) and the unload's caller is answered with the
reload's acknowledgement. B3's "never downgrade endingFor" guard goes,
as its commit said it would: it is safe now because the generation
decides -- an operator unload cancels the reload, so no new worker comes
and 'unload' is the truth -- and B3's other path, the discovery bound,
is still gated by `unloading !== true` (sandbox/27 passes). With no
worker registered yet, the pending spawn is ended and the devices the
reload marked are settled unloaded, so a job waiting through the reload
fails MODULE_UNLOADED at once, not after the 30 s wait. A supervisor
restart still stands down to a live worker: a restart racing an operator
reload leaves one worker. An operator restart takes its generation up
front, before it ends the old worker: an unload or reload arriving while
that worker is still acknowledging (up to 3 s) outranks it, and the
restart's continuation stands down with MODULE_LOAD_SUPERSEDED instead of
bringing the module back or outranking the later caller (review of
#22).

test/sandbox/33 (a module slow to load, 1.5 s, and to discover, 3 s,
under --moduleSandbox off): two reloads 300 ms apart -- the first
answers MODULE_LOAD_SUPERSEDED, the second 200, calls in between see
MODULE_RELOADING and never MODULE_UNLOADED or DEVICE_NOT_FOUND, and a
job added between them completes on the new worker; a reload then an
unload 300 ms later -- the unload answers 200, the reload
MODULE_LOAD_SUPERSEDED, the tools are gone and the device answers
MODULE_UNLOADED 5 s on, a job added between them fails MODULE_UNLOADED
within seconds and is not retried; the module loads again afterwards;
under audit, a supervisor restart racing an operator reload leaves one
worker and the device never answers DEVICE_NOT_FOUND; with the old
worker held 1.2 s, an unload 300 ms into a restart wins (the module
stays unloaded, the restart MODULE_LOAD_SUPERSEDED) and so does a
reload (its caller answered, one worker). Alive workers are
counted from the log ("spawn walk" against "settled"). Failed before
(the job failed MODULE_UNLOADED and calls saw it; the unload was refused
UNLOAD_MODULE_FAIL), passes now; the whole test/sandbox and
test/module-loading folders pass. MODULE_LOAD_SUPERSEDED is in both
error catalogues, the CHANGELOG and docs/module-development.md's "when
your module's worker ends".
